g.text: Worlds: a world is a place an agent can run, a machine or a container

text.tspan: A conversation is the thing people look at: a durable transcript with an id, living on the bus and folded into towerd's sqlite. A world is a place an agent can run, a machine or a container, named by whoever deployed it and never centrally registered. An agent instance is one process's presence in a world, the pair (world, instanceId); it claims a conversation by attaching to it, and a conversation is served by at most one instance at a time.

Users never address a world. They open a conversation in a client and say into it; asking a different world to serve that conversation is how work migrates between machines. Whether an instance is still alive is nobody's declaration: each client derives it from the last pulse against its own clock.

Nothing here is privileged. claude-sdk-cli is its own terminal agent with its own UI, written before any of this, and it takes part by publishing the same subjects everything else does: towerd folds its conversations beside the rest and never knows the difference. That is what the contract buys, and it is the test of whether the contract is real.
Colours: green = our services, teal = a separate implementation of the same contract, blue = clients, cyan = the bus, orange = worlds, purple = storage, gold = people, red = external.
owns sqlite on its own thread
hosts the agent, streams it onto the bus
a separate implementation of the same contract:
its own terminal UI and its own agent, publishing straight onto the bus
